name: How does a general contractor coordinate the trades needed for a bathroom addition?

mainEntity.name: How does a general contractor coordinate the trades needed for a bathroom addition?

acceptedAnswer.text: Bathroom additions require careful coordination between structural framing, licensed trade work, and finish detailing. An owner-operated finish contractor like HH Remodeling provides a single point of contact on site while managing licensed plumbing and electrical sub-trades for critical rough-ins. In-house crew members handle the custom framing, drywall installation, moisture-resistant backer boards, precision tile and marble setting, trim carpentry, and interior painting. This cohesive setup prevents communication gaps between trades, keeps timelines tight, and ensures finished surfaces—such as shower enclosures and custom vanities—are built on level, plumb framing.
acceptedAnswer.description: An owner-operated general contractor manages licensed plumbing and electrical rough-ins while directing on-site crews for framing, drywall, tile, trim, and painting.
